items.t: Falcon wing doors stop, won't open or hit objects
items.job: Diagnose and recalibrate or replace falcon wing door sensors
items.note: Owners report $300–$1,600; cracked door glass from a strike adds more.

items.t: Front doors won't open, close or latch
items.job: Replace front door latch(es)
items.note: Owners report about $1,100 (Canadian) for one latch and $1,808 for an updated latch retrofit with other work.

items.t: Shudder or vibration from front half-shafts
items.job: Replace both front half-shafts
items.note: Owners report about $1,770–$2,400 for both sides.

items.t: Air suspension won't inflate or sags
items.job: Replace leaking air strut(s) and compressor
items.note: Owners report $3,400–$4,500 when struts and the compressor are replaced together.

items.t: A/C stops cooling
items.job: Replace A/C compressor (and condenser if contaminated)
items.note: Owners report about $2,900 for a compressor and $4,700 when the condenser and evaporator are also replaced. Leaks and sensors cost far less.

items.t: Touchscreen goes blank from worn memory chip (recall 21V-035)
items.job: Recall repair or software update at Tesla
items.note: Free under the recall. Enter your VIN on Tesla's or NHTSA's recall lookup to check.

items.t: Center screen freezes or goes black
items.job: Replace media computer or upgrade to MCU2
items.note: Owners report about $300 for a navigation memory card, $670 (Canadian) for an MCU, and around $2,400 for an MCU2 upgrade plus charger.

items.t: 12-volt battery fails
items.job: Replace 12-volt battery
items.note: Owners report about $200–$220.

items.t: Front control arms squeak or links break
items.job: Replace front control arms or aft link
items.note: Model X owners mostly report these under warranty; Model S owners paid about $1,100 for a pair of upper arms.

items.t: Battery coolant leak
items.job: Repair coolant leak and refill
items.note: One owner paid about $520 (Canadian).
